headline: Facebook lets you customize your feed with AI, mirroring Instagram
summary: Meta is rolling out the 'Your Algorithm' feature to Facebook, allowing users to directly manage content preferences and leverage LLMs for real-time feed adjustments.
details: Facebook is introducing a new feature called "Your Algorithm," which mirrors Instagram's functionality, enabling users to directly control the topics they see in their feed and Reels.
Users can mark topics as "interested" or "not interested" via a three-dot menu on posts or directly under content. Meta states that recommendations will update in real time based on these selections.
This feature is part of Meta's broader strategy to enhance user experience through AI-powered tools. The company is increasingly integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into its ranking systems.

LLMs can now understand the nuances of natural language, allowing users to express their content preferences more effectively. This means users can tell the algorithm what they want to see more or less of, and their feed will adapt accordingly within the same session.

Meta has already launched similar features on other platforms, including "Your Algorithm" on Instagram and a "Dear Algo" feature on Threads, indicating a consistent approach to user-driven content curation across its social media ecosystem.
caption:
Tired of the algorithm dictating your feed? Facebook is giving you the reins with its new 'Your Algorithm' feature, powered by AI.

Facebook is introducing a new feature called "Your Algorithm," which mirrors Instagram's functionality, enabling users to directly control the topics they see in their feed and Reels.

Users can mark topics as "interested" or "not interested" via a three-dot menu on posts or directly under content. Meta states that recommendations will update in real time based on these selections.

This feature is part of Meta's broader strategy to enhance user experience through AI-powered tools. The company is increasingly integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into its ranking systems.

LLMs can now understand the nuances of natural language, allowing users to express their content preferences more effectively. This means users can tell the algorithm what they want to see more or less of, and their feed will adapt accordingly within the same session.

Meta has already launched similar features on other platforms, including "Your Algorithm" on Instagram and a "Dear Algo" feature on Threads, indicating a consistent approach to user-driven content curation across its social media ecosystem.
